nodes.summary: Let $N$ be a list of natural numbers, $w$ a list of booleans and $C$ a CNF clause. The check of $C$ against $N$ and $w$ returns true if and only if $C$ is satisfied by the assignment that sends each natural number $x$ to the value returned by looking up $x$ in $N$ and $w$.
nodes.title: Correctness of the witness clause check

nodes.summary: Let $N$ be a list of natural numbers, $w$ a list of booleans and $C$ a CNF clause, viewed as a list of $\ell$ literals (repetitions counted). The cost of checking $C$ against $N$ and $w$ is at most $\ell \cdot (|N| + 1)$, where $|N|$ is the length of $N$.
nodes.title: Cost bound for the witness clause check

nodes.summary: Given a list $N$ of natural numbers, a list $w$ of booleans and a CNF clause $C$, the check of $C$ against $N$ and $w$ is the timed computation (a returned boolean together with a natural-number cost) that scans the literals $(x, b)$ of $C$ in order: for each it charges one tick, then looks up $x$ in $N$ and $w$, paying the cost of the lookup, and returns true if the value found equals the polarity $b$; otherwise…
nodes.title: Clause check against a witness

nodes.summary: Let $N$ be a list of natural numbers, $w$ a list of booleans and $\varphi$ a CNF formula. The check of $\varphi$ against $N$ and $w$ returns true if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfied by the assignment that sends each natural number $x$ to the value returned by looking up $x$ in $N$ and $w$.
nodes.title: Correctness of the witness formula check

nodes.summary: Let $N$ be a list of natural numbers, $w$ a list of booleans and $\varphi$ a CNF formula, and let $L$ be the sum of the lengths of the clauses of $\varphi$ (its total number of literals). The cost of checking $\varphi$ against $N$ and $w$ is at most $L \cdot (|N| + 1)$, where $|N|$ is the length of $N$.
nodes.title: Cost bound for the witness formula check

nodes.summary: Given a list $N$ of natural numbers, a list $w$ of booleans and a CNF formula $\varphi$, the check of $\varphi$ against $N$ and $w$ is the timed computation that runs the clause check against $N$ and $w$ on the clauses of $\varphi$ in order, adding up their costs, and returns false as soon as one of them returns false. If every clause check returns true, in particular if $\varphi$ has no clauses, it returns true.
nodes.title: Formula check against a witness

nodes.summary: Let $v$ be a function from the natural numbers to the booleans, $N = (n_1, \dots, n_k)$ a list of natural numbers and $x$ a natural number. Looking up $x$ in $N$ and the list $(v(n_1), \dots, v(n_k))$ returns $v(x)$ if $x$ occurs in $N$, and false otherwise.
nodes.title: Lookup in the witness of an assignment

nodes.summary: For every list $N$ of natural numbers, every list $w$ of booleans and every natural number $x$, the cost of looking up $x$ in $N$ and $w$ is at most the length of $N$.
nodes.title: Cost bound for witness lookup

nodes.summary: Given a list $N = (n_1, \dots, n_k)$ of natural numbers, a list $w = (b_1, \dots, b_m)$ of booleans and a natural number $x$, the lookup of $x$ in $N$ and $w$ is the timed computation (a returned boolean together with a natural-number cost) that scans the pairs $(n_1, b_1), (n_2, b_2), \dots$ in order, charging one tick for each pair it examines, and returns $b_i$ for the first $i$ with $n_i = x$; if either list…
nodes.title: Witness lookup

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula, $C$ a clause of $\varphi$ and $(x, b)$ a literal of $C$. Then $x$ belongs to the list of variables occurring in $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Variables of a formula occur in its occurrence list

nodes.summary: If the function sending a pair $(x, w)$ of lists of Booleans to the Boolean returned by the SAT verifier on $(x, w)$ is polynomial-time computable, by a multi-stack Turing machine under the canonical bitstring encodings, then the SAT decision problem belongs to NP.
nodes.title: SAT is in NP if its verifier is polynomial-time

nodes.summary: For all lists of Booleans $x$ and $w$, if the complete CNF decoder fails on $x$, then the SAT verifier on $(x, w)$ returns false at declared time cost $0$.
nodes.title: The SAT verifier rejects undecodable inputs

nodes.summary: For all lists of Booleans $x$ and $w$ and every CNF formula $\varphi$, if the complete CNF decoder returns $\varphi$ on $x$, then the SAT verifier on $(x, w)$ coincides with the CNF check of $\varphi$ against the witness $w$ and the occurrence list of $\varphi$: both the returned Boolean and the declared time cost are the same.
nodes.title: The SAT verifier on a decodable input

nodes.summary: For all lists of Booleans $x$ (the input) and $w$ (the witness), the declared time cost of the SAT verifier on $(x, w)$ is at most $N^2 + N$, where $N = |x| + |w|$ is the sum of their lengths.
nodes.title: Declared time bound of the SAT verifier

nodes.summary: There is a polynomial $q$ with natural number coefficients such that for all lists of Booleans $x$ (the input) and $w$ (the witness), the declared time cost of the SAT verifier on $(x, w)$ is at most $q(|x| + |w|)$.
nodes.title: The SAT verifier has polynomial declared time

nodes.summary: The SAT verifier verifies the SAT decision problem with witness bound the polynomial $X$: for every list $x$ of Booleans, $x$ encodes a satisfiable CNF formula if and only if there is a list $w$ of Booleans, of length at most the length of $x$, such that the SAT verifier on $(x, w)$ returns true.
nodes.title: The SAT verifier verifies SAT

nodes.summary: The SAT verifier takes a pair $(x, w)$ of lists of Booleans, an input $x$ and a witness $w$, and returns a Boolean together with a declared time cost. If the complete CNF decoder fails on $x$, it returns false at cost $0$. If $x$ decodes to a CNF formula $\varphi$, it returns the result and the cost of the CNF check of $\varphi$ against the witness $w$ and the occurrence list of $\varphi$, so that $w$ is read as…
nodes.title: The SAT verifier

nodes.summary: For every CNF formula $\varphi$, the sum over the clauses of $\varphi$ of their lengths (the total number of literals of $\varphi$) is at most the length of the length-prefixed binary code of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: The literal count is at most the code length

nodes.summary: For every CNF formula $\varphi$, the length of the occurrence list of $\varphi$ equals the total number of literals of $\varphi$, that is, the sum over the clauses of $\varphi$ of their lengths.
nodes.title: Length of the occurrence list

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi = (C_1, \dots, C_m)$, the occurrence list of $\varphi$ is the list of the variable indices of its literals, in order: the variables of the literals of $C_1$ in order, then those of $C_2$, and so on up to $C_m$. Duplicates are kept, so a variable appears once for each literal in which it occurs.
nodes.title: Occurrence list of a CNF formula
